questions.stem: Bí o bá kọ ìwé sí àjọ atúnlùútò, irú àròkọ tí o kọ ni
questions.explanation: Writing to an organisation (a travel agency) is a letter: àròkọ onílẹ́tà (a formal letter).

questions.stem: Èwo ni ó jẹmọ́ àròkọ aṣàpèjúwe?
questions.explanation: 'Ààfin ọba ìlú mi' (the king's palace in my town) calls for description of a place: a descriptive essay (aṣàpèjúwe); the others are proverbs/arguments or a narrative.

questions.stem: "Iṣẹ́ akadá ṣòro" jẹmọ́ àròkọ
questions.explanation: 'Academic work is difficult' is a debatable claim to be argued for or against: an argumentative essay (aṣàríyànjiyàn).

questions.stem: Àfẹ̀gbẹ́-ẹnu-pè ni
questions.explanation: [l] is the lateral sound (àfẹ̀gbẹ́-ẹnu-pè): air escapes along the sides of the tongue; [r] is a flap/trill, [w] a semivowel and [f] a fricative.

questions.stem: Ọ̀nà iṣẹnupè ni
questions.explanation: Àsénupè (stop/plosive) describes the manner of articulation; the other options (bilabial, alveolar, labiodental) are places of articulation.

questions.stem: Fáwẹ̀lì roboto ni
questions.explanation: [u] is pronounced with rounded lips (fáwẹ̀lì roboto); [i], [a] and [e] are unrounded (pẹrẹsẹ).

questions.stem: Ìhun sílébù 'àgbébọ̀' ni
questions.explanation: à-gbé-bọ̀: a vowel (F), then consonant + vowel (KF), then consonant + vowel (KF): F-KF-KF; 'gb' is a single consonant.

questions.stem: Ọ̀rọ̀-orúkọ aṣeékà ni
questions.explanation: Ẹsẹ̀ (leg/foot) can be counted (ẹsẹ̀ méjì); sand, water and flood water are uncountable nouns.

questions.stem: "Mo lọ sí ilé kíákíá", 'kíákíá' jẹ́
questions.explanation: Kíákíá (quickly) tells how the action of 'lọ' was done, so it is an adverb (ọ̀rọ̀-àpọ́nlé).

questions.stem: "Aṣọ Olú ti ya", 'Olú' jẹ́ ẹ̀yán
questions.explanation: In 'aṣọ Olú', the noun Olú qualifies (shows the owner of) the noun aṣọ, so it is a noun-qualifier (ẹ̀yán ajórúkọ).

questions.stem: Nínú "èmi yóò lọ", 'yóò' jẹ́ atọ́ka
questions.explanation: Yóò marks an action that will take place later: future tense (àsìkò ọjọ́-iwájú).

questions.stem: "Ire wà nínú ibi" jẹ́ àpẹẹrẹ gbólóhùn
questions.explanation: The sentence simply makes a statement; it is not a command, question or emphatic construction, so it is a declarative sentence (gbólóhùn àlàyé).

questions.stem:
Túmọ̀ ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan gbólóhùn wọ̀nyí sí èdè Yorùbá.

He sings while working.
options: Ó máa ń kọrin bí ó bá ń ṣiṣẹ́.
Ó máa ń kọrin níbi iṣẹ́ rẹ̀.
Ó máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ bí ó bá ń kọrin.
Ó máa ń ṣiṣẹ́ níbi tí ó ti ń kọrin.
questions.explanation: The main action is singing (kọrin) and it happens while (bí ó bá ń) he is working (ṣiṣẹ́).

questions.stem:
Túmọ̀ ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan gbólóhùn wọ̀nyí sí èdè Yorùbá.

He has been elevated.
questions.explanation: The passive 'has been elevated' is rendered with the impersonal subject 'A': A ti gbé e ga (he has been raised up).

questions.stem:
Túmọ̀ ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan gbólóhùn wọ̀nyí sí èdè Yorùbá.

The committee was reminded to be punctual.
options: A rán ìgbìmọ̀ náà létí láti wá.
A rán ìgbìmọ̀ náà létí láti tún wá.
A rán ìgbìmọ̀ náà létí láti tètè dé.
A rán ìgbìmọ̀ náà létí láti dé.
questions.explanation: 'To be punctual' is 'láti tètè dé' (to arrive early/on time); the other options leave out punctuality.

questions.stem:
Túmọ̀ ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan gbólóhùn wọ̀nyí sí èdè Yorùbá.

The driver lost control of the vehicle.
options: Awakọ̀ kò lè darí ọkọ̀ náà mọ́.
Awakọ̀ náà kò mọ ọwọ́ ọkọ̀ náà.
questions.explanation: 'Lost control' means he could no longer steer/direct the vehicle: kò lè darí ọkọ̀ náà mọ́.

questions.stem: "Ilé Akin gba gbogbo ayé" jẹ́ àpẹẹrẹ
questions.explanation: Saying a house occupies the whole world is deliberate exaggeration: àsọrégèé (hyperbole).

questions.stem: Òrìṣà wo ni à ń pè ní 'Olóde'?
questions.explanation: Ṣànpọ̀nná, the smallpox deity, is euphemistically called Olóde (owner of the outside).

questions.stem: Èwo ni orúkọ tí à ń fún àbíkú?
questions.explanation: Kílàńkó ('what is left to be cut?') refers to the marks cut on an àbíkú; Ìdòwú is the child born after twins, Àjàyí a child born face-down, and Ọdẹ́rìndé a name from a hunter's family.

questions.stem: ........ ni a fi ń se gbẹ̀gìrì.
questions.explanation: Gbẹ̀gìrì is a soup made from peeled, mashed beans (erèé/ẹ̀wà).

questions.stem: Ẹni tó ń fi eégún mọ̀nà ni à ń pè ní
questions.explanation: The atọ́kùn guides (leads) the masquerade, who cannot see the way clearly.

questions.stem: Èwo ló jẹmọ́ iṣẹ́ àgbẹ̀dẹ?
questions.explanation: Ẹwìrì (the bellows) is used by the blacksmith (alágbẹ̀dẹ) to fan the fire of the forge; apáṣá is a weaver's tool.

questions.stem: Èwo ló tóbi jù nínú àwọn wọ̀nyí?
questions.explanation: Dàńdógó is the largest, most flowing type of agbádá; gbárìyẹ̀ and ṣapará are smaller styles.

questions.stem: "Àrẹdú o" là ń kí
questions.explanation: Àrẹdú o ('may the dye turn deep/black') is the greeting for the dyer (aláró), whose indigo must darken.

questions.stem:
Kọ àròkọ tí kò dín ní 300 ẹyọ ọ̀rọ̀ lórí orí-ọ̀rọ̀ kan ṣoṣo tí o bá yàn. Máṣe lò ju ìṣẹ́jú márùn-úndínláàádọ́ta lórí abala yìí. Èdè Yorùbá ni kí o fi dáhùn gbogbo ìbéèrè kí o sì lo àkọtọ́ òde òní àti èdè-Ìperí Yorùbá.
(a) Ènìyàn ṣòro
(b) Pàtàkì ètò ìròyìn ní àwùjọ wa
(d) Ìlù
(e) Ìwúlò epo pupa
(ẹ) Kọ lẹ́tà sí àbúrò rẹ tí ó wà ní òkè-òkun láti ròyìn ayẹyẹ ìgbéyàwó ẹ̀gbọ́n yín tí ó wáyé láìpẹ́ yìí.
questions.markingGuide:
7 marks: Akoonu (content) — relevant, well-developed points on the chosen topic, e.g. (b) news informs, educates, entertains, warns of danger and connects government with the people; (e) palm oil is used for cooking, soap and pomade making, medicine, lamps and trade; (ẹ) a lively account of the wedding (introduction, engagement/ìdána, church/mosque, reception, gifts) with family news
5 marks: Ètò (organisation) — suitable title, introduction, logical paragraphs and conclusion; for (ẹ) the features of an informal letter: address and date, greeting (e.g. Àbúrò mi ọ̀wọ́n), body, closing and first name
10 marks: Ìlò èdè (expression) — idiomatic, natural Yoruba with apt proverbs (òwe), idioms (àkànlò-èdè) and varied sentences; no English words or literal translation from English
3 marks: Àkọtọ́ (mechanical accuracy) — correct modern Yoruba orthography, tone marks and sub-dots, spelling and punctuation
questions.explanation: Model answer outline for (ẹ): Writer's address and date; 'Àbúrò mi ọ̀wọ́n,' then greetings and enquiry after his/her health abroad. The letter describes how the elder sibling's wedding took place: the ìdána/engagement in which the groom's family brought the customary items, prayers by elders, the church/mosque ceremony, the colourful aṣọ-ẹbí, drumming and dancing at the reception, and how the bride was escorted to her husband's house. It mentions those who asked after the reader, uses a suitable proverb (e.g. 'Ilé ọkọ ilé ẹ̀kọ́'), urges him/her to study hard, and closes 'Ìwọ ni tìrẹ,' followed by the writer's first name. Other options are handled as expository/descriptive essays in correct modern Yoruba orthography.
